newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shippers seek KLM surcharge meeting.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shippers seek KLM surcharge meeting.

text.p: EVO, the Dutch shippers association, is inviting KLM Cargo boss, Jacques Ancher, for a meeting about the carrier's introduction of a fuel surcharge, said EVO secretary, Hans Leijgraaff.
"Even though we have written to the Dutch government about this issue, we are in favour of self-regulation, hence the meeting with KLM," he said.
KLM Cargo introduced a 20 Dutch guilder cents per kilo fuel surcharge on November 1.
Since that time 20 other carriers in the Dutch market have followed, said Leijgraaff.
"In the meeting with KLM the shippers want to discuss delaying the surcharge or reimbursing shippers instead. And they want to know when it is going to end," he added.
"We also want to discuss hardship cases with KLM," he said.
Already there have been some meetings between KLM and shippers, he said. "Some of the largest shippers (in the top ten) have had meetings but these have been useless."
The KLM representatives were at too low a level to make decisions on this issue and they had not been briefed properly, he added.
"In theory every shipper is unwilling to pay these surcharges but they are well aware that the carriers can refuse to take their cargo," he said when commenting on whether surcharges will be paid.
"We know the fuel prices have increased, that it not the issue, it is the way the charges have been implemented," he stated. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
